# The Japan Breach Registry 2026 — 2026年秋、日本の企業・組織を襲った個人情報漏えいの波

> An append-only registry by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史), AI Strategist, of
> personal-data breaches disclosed by Japanese companies and organisations on
> or after 1 September 2026. Only breaches whose primary notice the author
> opened and read are admitted; each row keeps the notice's own unit (records,
> persons, accounts) and wording (confirmed, possible, cannot be ruled out,
> maximum) and classifies the vector only as far as the notice states it. The
> first edition (10 October 2026) carries 31 rows and holds 16 further cases
> outside the ledger as "pending verification." The second edition (16 October
> 2026) carries 36 rows and holds 11 cases pending. The third edition (26 October
> 2026) carries 71 rows and holds 25 cases pending. The fourth edition (3 November
> 2026) carries 300 rows and holds 67 cases pending. The fifth edition (8 November
> 2026, extended on 10 November 2026) carries 584 rows and holds 110 cases
> pending. The sixth edition (14 November 2026) carries 844 rows and holds
> 120 cases pending. Alongside the ledger, the book
> sorts every claim that "attackers used AI" into four tiers — evidence, trace,
> possibility, no mention — and tests eight candidate explanations for why the
> autumn of 2026 concentrated in Japan on identical criteria. As of the first
> edition, no Japanese case reaches the evidence tier and none of the eight
> explanations is supported for Japan. The book does not claim that AI caused
> the wave, that Claude Mythos was used, that Glasswing-disclosed
> vulnerabilities were exploited, or that the Japanese and Korean attackers
> are the same, because no primary source says so. Central question: in a
> world where AI has collapsed the cost of finding vulnerabilities, does the
> defender's head start hold?

## Key facts (first edition, 2026-10-10)

- Tokyo Shoko Research (7 Oct 2026): breaches of 1 million+ records at listed companies and subsidiaries: 10 in 2026 as of 5 Oct (6 in all of 2025); breaches of 10 million+: 3 in the fourteen years to 2025, 3 in 2026 alone.
- JPCERT/CC (8 Oct 2026): breaches "相次いでいます" (have followed one another) around September 2026, while available technical information is "限定的かつ断片的" (limited and fragmentary). The alert contains no reference to AI.
- Ledger: 31 rows; 8 exceed one million in the notice's own unit; 14 notices state the vector (vulnerability 5, VPN vulnerability 1, contractor 5, unauthorised login 1, misconfiguration 1, multiple 1), 17 do not; 0 notices mention attacker-side AI.
- (Added 16 October 2026) Ledger: 36 rows, 11 pending. Five pending cases admitted (032 Bookoff Group Holdings, 033 Daiwa Securities, 034 Sagawa Express, 035 Uzabase/NewsPicks, 036 White Essence). 10 rows exceed one million in the notice's own unit; 16 notices state the vector (vulnerability 6, VPN vulnerability 1, contractor 6, unauthorised login 1, misconfiguration 1, multiple 1), 20 do not; 0 notices mention attacker-side AI. A third contractor chain: Scala Communications (022) → Daiwa Securities (033). Follow-ups recorded as dated corrections: 018 GMO Research & AI confirmed 894,082 records taken out (first notice: up to 948,498); 019 Kufu confirmed 308 customers; 023 IDC Frontier judged no data exfiltration (5th notice, 14 Oct); 027 JR East received the contractor's report of no leak (15 Oct).
- Two contractor chains: IDC Frontier (ransomware, 7 Oct, 495 contracting organisations) → JR East; Commune → WingArc1st, Sansan, LIXIL.
- (Added 26 October 2026) Ledger: 71 rows, 25 pending. 35 rows added (037–071): 6 from pending (Shueisha, JAEA, Study Sapuri, Nikkei, Viewcard, JR Kyushu) and 29 disclosed 16–24 Oct (SourceNext 22,519,960; Capcom 11,774,247; Yumirlink approx. 9 million cumulative; Trustbank 4,454,097; Lindt 3,147,469; and ST approx. 2.5 million; Nikkei approx. 1.83 million; Yamato Transport approx. 5.26 million; FANCL/Attenir 785,496 persons; Crypton 362,137; Digital Agency via Studio; MLIT; NEC → Osaka University 77,851; Rakus/blastmail → Tokyo Metropolitan Government, Cells; Yumirlink → Nomura Securities; and others). 21 rows exceed one million, 5 exceed ten million (005, 028, 017, 044, 064); 36 notices state the vector (vulnerability 12, VPN 1, contractor 16, unauthorised login 4, misconfiguration 2, multiple 1), 35 do not; 0 notices mention attacker-side AI; 3 mention defender-side AI (005, 054, 062). Seven contractor chains; the five new ones start at a SaaS (Studio, Yumirlink, blastmail, NEC, FutureShop). Follow-ups: 007 Times Mobility 5th notice (23 Oct) fixed 6,628,007 records and 1,464,800 ID images and disclosed the vector as a web-system vulnerability; 025 Lawson (24 Oct) removed email addresses and added date of birth; 028 skyticket 2nd notice (16 Oct) card data up to 6,140 persons; 034 Sagawa 5th notice (23 Oct, unread, press: up to approx. 53.23 million).
- (Added 26 October 2026) Evidence tier, Japan: JPCERT/CC Eyes (15 Oct 2026), investigation of attack-source servers: 「攻撃者がAIを利用して、既知の脆弱性のスキャンやAPI経由での攻撃などを実施していたことを確認しました」; servers also attacked services outside Japan; APK analysis and SSRF probing found on the servers. NorForge (19 Oct 2026): exposed Cairn panels, cluster AIA0001 "mostly in the US, Japan and Australia," worker "claudecode_deepseek-v4.1-flash," a "Japanese retailer" case. Trace tier: JPCERT/CC alert updated 23 Oct 2026, Case E: 「CairnやCyberStrikeAI、ARTEXなどのAIを用いたペネトレーションテスト基盤を悪用した攻撃試行が確認されています」; Secure Sky Technology (14 Oct): at least 3 IPs running AI-agent attacks on Japanese sites, model unknown; GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae (19 Oct, press-based): ARTEX on attack infrastructure targeting approx. 20 Japanese companies. Possibility: Cyber Security Cloud (9 Oct), NICT A2B attack (13 Oct). Macnica (7 Oct): no logs or traces proving AI. NCO (9 Oct): "AI の悪用を含む" as a general statement. No mention: all 71 Japanese notices.
- (Added 3 November 2026) Ledger: 300 rows, 67 pending. 229 rows added (072–300): 14 from pending and 215 disclosed 9 Oct – 2 Nov 2026 (largest: Ryohin Keikaku/MUJI up to approx. 27.26 million; Nojima approx. 7 million; Prestige International up to approx. 5.5 million; Club Tourism approx. 4.32 million; Hana Cupid 4,238,242; Recruit Carsensor.net up to 3,709,551; istyle approx. 3 million persons; Matsuya Foods 2,377,127; So-net 2,141,986). 38 rows exceed one million, 6 exceed ten million (005, 028, 017, 044, 064, 275); 226 notices state the vector (contractor 179, vulnerability 27, unauthorised login 12, multiple 4, misconfiguration 3, VPN 1), 74 do not; 163 of the 229 new rows are contractor rows. More than twenty contractor chains (blastmail 29, Studio 26, Commune 18, Yumirlink 18, Arara 11, NTT DATA bond-perk service 6, Amadeus 7, others). Follow-ups: 053 Yumirlink 2nd notice (26 Oct) 51,628,280 cumulative across 49 systems; 028 skyticket 3rd notice (30 Oct) 32,341 bank-account records leaked; 023 IDC Frontier 7th notice (27 Oct) vector disclosed as an OSS vulnerability; 047 Comic Cmoa up to approx. 4.2 million log records.
- (Added 3 November 2026) First victim notice mentioning attacker-side AI about its own incident: 079 Chitose Group (via Commune), 「攻撃は、複数のIPアドレスから短時間に大量の操作を同時に行うものでした。このことから、AI等を用いて自動化された攻撃であったと推定されます。」 Tier 3 (possibility): a presumption based on the attack's shape; the presumer is not stated. No mention: 299 of 300 notices.
- (Added 8 November 2026) Ledger: 507 rows, 91 pending. 207 rows added (301–507): 14 from pending, 184 disclosed 3–7 Nov 2026, 9 disclosed 8 Oct – 2 Nov missed by v4.0 (largest: GMO Makeshop approx. 12.6 million; BK Japan approx. 11.18 million; MOS Food Services 7,517,087; Plenus up to approx. 7 million; WILLs/NetMile up to approx. 5.49 million persons; TKC up to 2,230,812; SignalTalk 1,855,578; Workman up to approx. 1.45 million). 49 rows exceed one million, 8 exceed ten million (005, 028, 017, 044, 064, 275, 304, 484); 418 notices state the vector (contractor 356, vulnerability 32, unauthorised login 16, multiple 7, misconfiguration 6, VPN 1), 89 do not; 177 of the 207 new rows (86%) are contractor rows and 137 descend from one intrusion at Arara's mail-delivery services (55 via TKC, municipal My Number Card / online-application systems). Arara 3rd notice (6 Nov): "81,329,467 (approx. 81 million)" de-duplicated, up to approx. 380 client companies, vector not disclosed. 83 rows disclosed on 4 Nov, the largest single day. New chains: SMBC Consumer Finance guarantee system (12 partner banks), Prestige International (JA Kyosai, Nissan Financial Services, KDDI), CBcloud PickGo (Seven-Eleven Japan, Demae-can), Securitize Japan, Arcadia SpeeCAN RAIDEN, Shibata Koji Chosa ransomware. Follow-ups: 004 Rohto 2,797,545 customers and vector (telephone-system credentials); 215 Paydon up to 257,639; 275 Ryohin Keikaku 2nd notice. Independent intrusions approx. 180, vector known for approx. 60. No mention of attacker-side AI: 506 of 507 notices. Chapter 5 judgements not revisited in v5.0.
- (Added 10 November 2026) Ledger: 584 rows, 110 pending. 77 rows added (508–584): 5 from pending, 64 disclosed 6–9 Nov 2026, 8 disclosed 30 Oct – 5 Nov missed earlier (largest: Nitori Holdings up to 37.62 million, now the largest row; Sharefull up to approx. 7.5 million personal accounts; SEGA 2,196,044; Shogakukan 1,993,665; Hotelovers 1,578,779). 54 rows exceed one million, 9 exceed ten million (005, 028, 017, 044, 064, 275, 304, 484, 577); 482 notices state the vector (contractor 417, vulnerability 33, unauthorised login 18, multiple 7, misconfiguration 6, VPN 1), 102 do not. New contractor rows: Arara 30, Prestige Core Solution 17, SMBC Consumer Finance guarantee system 5 (7 banks), new chain LENDY Servicer 2. No new notice mentions attacker-side AI about its own incident; no mention: 583 of 584. Verification of the fifth edition: the author read the notices of 9 rows (301–309); AI agents re-fetched and checked the other 275 (310–584) against the notices, correcting 8 rows; 3 could not be re-fetched.
- (Added 14 November 2026) Ledger: 844 rows, 120 pending. 260 rows added (585–844): 24 from pending, 128 disclosed 10–13 Nov 2026, 108 disclosed 7 Sep – 9 Nov missed earlier (largest: Iris Plaza approx. 7.7 million people; Arcadia approx. 3.136 million email addresses, an estimate; Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry up to approx. 1.97 million records; Yeny 1,332,505; Kawajun 1,214,183). 60 rows exceed one million, 9 exceed ten million; 719 notices state the vector, 125 do not; 224 of the 260 new rows (86%) via a contractor (new chain origins: OPENLOGI, teket, Fireworks AI as Notion's AI processor). No new row mentions attacker-side AI (843 of 844 no mention). Notices of 14 November not yet captured.
- (Corrected 10 November 2026) Admission criterion: From the fifth edition, the admission criterion is that the organisation's own primary notice was reached and its text confirms the case is in scope (a breach, or possible breach, of personal data through external unauthorised access). AI agents retrieve and check the notices, recording verbatim the sentences used as evidence; the author spot-checks notices and decides rows on the boundary of the criteria. The 300 rows up to the fourth edition are rows whose notice the author opened and read.
- (Corrected 3 November 2026) Chapter 1: "not the count, but the size" does not hold for October. Trend Micro (16 Oct 2026, primary): 607 incidents of all types in Jan–Sep 2026 (2.2/day; unauthorised access 331); 「2026年10月は1週目（10月1～9日分）のみで、52件に上ります」; "data supply-chain" cases 62 (10.2%). 170 of the ledger's 268 October rows are contractor rows. Collapsing chains, 300 rows ≈ 144 independent intrusions; the vector is disclosed for about a third. Tokyo Shoko Research (23 Oct 2026): 10-million-plus breaches at listed companies 「すでに8件（速報値）」 by 23 Oct. Chapter 5: H7 "leaning refuted for large rows" withdrawn (028 skyticket 3rd notice 「不正に取得された認証情報が悪用され」; 290 Prestige; 053 Yumirlink) — credentials taken in the intrusion, market link undetermined; H3 contractor skew supported for the whole period; H4 succession of mail-delivery SaaS breaches observed, single attacker undetermined. No candidate is now "leaning refuted"; none is supported as the cause of the ledger's breaches.
- (Added 26 October 2026) Chapter 5 verdicts: H1 Japan — attacker-side AI use supported (JPCERT/CC), link to ledger rows undetermined; H3 — contractor/SaaS concentration supported for late October; H4 — multiple attack servers confirmed by JPCERT/CC, single group press-based only, Japan–Korea undetermined; H5 Japan — tool diffusion and attack attempts supported (JPCERT/CC), link to rows undetermined; H6 — no primary source (JPCERT/CC Case C cites CVE-2026-72898 Metabase, no Glasswing link); H7 — 4 unauthorised-login rows, large cases still not; H2, H8 unchanged. Chapter 6: CyberStrikeAI (Team Cymru, 2 Mar 2026) and Cairn (Gambit Security 22 Sep 2026; NorForge 19 Oct 2026) added beside ARTEX; no new Anthropic primary after 6 Oct.
- Evidence tier: CrowdStrike Intelligence (7 Oct 2026), South Korean financial sector: "Analysis of threat actor-controlled open directories uncovered Claude Code session histories"; ARTEX "used DeepSeek v4.1-flash as the primary LLM backend"; campaign "active from late September to early October 2026"; attribution "made with moderate confidence"; affected organisations "remains unconfirmed."
- Trace tier: Trend Micro's own text (8 Oct 2026): "現状、必ずしもこれらの攻撃がAIを直接的に用いたものであるという証拠があるわけではありませんが、ログだけ見ても「これまでとは違う挙動」を捉えていることは事実です。"
- ARTEX: GitHub releases v0.1.0 on 26 July 2026, v0.3.14 on 24 September 2026; 17 stars as of 10 October 2026.
- Project Glasswing: announced 7 April 2026 ("giving defenders a durable advantage"; Claude Mythos Preview "a general-purpose, unreleased frontier model"); initial update 22 May ("more than ten thousand" vulnerabilities; 530 disclosed, 75 patched, 65 public advisories); 6 October: "at least 129,000 verified software vulnerabilities between April and July 2026."

## Structure

- Prologue: 7 October — two documents on the same day
- Chapter 1: The anomaly of scale — not the count, but the size
- Chapter 2: A map of vectors — not one hole, but many
- Chapter 3: Four tiers of evidence — who said what, and how far
- Chapter 4: The ledger (31 rows; 16 pending — 36 rows; 11 pending as of 2026-10-16 — 71 rows; 25 pending as of 2026-10-26 — 300 rows; 67 pending as of 2026-11-03 — 507 rows; 91 pending as of 2026-11-08 — 584 rows; 110 pending as of 2026-11-10 — 844 rows; 120 pending as of 2026-11-14)
- Chapter 5: Eight explanations — supported, refuted, undetermined
- Chapter 6: The defender's bet — Glasswing's timeline and ARTEX's
- Chapter 7: Japan as an observation point — what can and cannot be said
- Epilogue: The ledger does not close
